text:
Mia (Marketing): Quick sync — we need final copy and two chart variants for the benchmark launch post. The story should land both PLG and enterprise buyers: latency vs cost tradeoffs + concrete callouts for Dedicated/Private. Thoughts on axes/annotations?

Ben (Growth): Two charts I think: 1) median latency (ms) on x vs cost per 1k tokens ($) on y — simple scatter with model/workload points. 2) a complementary tail-latency chart (CDF or 95/99 pctl lines) to show SLA risk. Keep copy focused on 'predictable economics'.

Sam (Data): Can provide numbers. I'll run the extract for chat, summarization, and embedding slices. For chart 1 I'd recommend log-scale on cost (y) if we include quantized variants, otherwise linear is fine. Suggested axes labels: x = median tail latency (ms), y = cost per 1k tokens ($). Also include small callout markers for "Prefix cache on" and "Quantized" variants.

Olivia (Design): @Mia @Ben ok on visual style: grayscale base, single accent color for Redwood highlight. For annotations: shorthand copy like "~2x unit cost reduction with prefix cache" and "99th percentile latency halved on Dedicated" — we can add small tooltip text in web version. Avoid clutter; use subtle arrows + boxed callouts.

Raj (Product): Positioning note: the narrative should be "Predictable latency. Predictable cost." Emphasize operational controls (batching, cache, quantization) that move points on the chart, not just raw model numbers. Also call out fallback behavior: when capacity constrained, requests route to compatible variants — helps enterprise trust.

Ben (Growth): Copy options we can test: A) "Predictable latency. Predictable cost." B) "Spend less, serve faster, stay online." I prefer A for headline and B as a supporting blurb if we need emotion.

Mia (Marketing): I like A as headline. Can we A/B headline in the email/web hero? Also we need 2 short captions under chart: one PLG-focused (bench highlights for engineers) and one enterprise-focused (SLA and fallbacks).

Sam (Data): Pasting tiny CSV snippet for Olivia to mock with — columns: workload, model_variant, median_ms, p95_ms, cost_per_1k_usd

Sam (Data): ```
workload,model_variant,median_ms,p95_ms,cost_per_1k_usd
chat,redwood-quant,42,180,0.012
chat,redwood-quant+cache,28,120,0.008
summarize,open-gt3,120,600,0.045
embed,embed-small,18,40,0.006
```

Olivia (Design): Nice. I'll mock two treatments tonight — scatter + callout and tail CDF with shaded SLA bands. Uploading to Drive. @DeployBot please paste link when ready.

DeployBot: New assets uploaded to https://drive.redwood.dev/bench/1704501234 (charts_v1/*).

Raj (Product): One more ask: include a tiny footnote about measurement conditions (seq length, tokenization, hardware) so we don't get pulled on apples-to-oranges. Something like: "Median measured on A100-like GPU, tokenization=byte-pair, sample workloads described above."

Mia (Marketing): Perfect — action items: Sam -> finalize CSV + short methods blurb; Olivia -> two mockups (scatter + tail) with accent palette; Ben -> two headline variants for A/B; Raj -> one-sentence product blurb on fallbacks. I'll stitch final copy and send draft for review by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:

Ben (Growth): Happy to review the A/B assets tomorrow morning.

Sam (Data): I'll drop the full dataset and a short note on measurement into the Drive folder in 1 hour.

Olivia (Design): I'll ping here when mocks are done.

Mia (Marketing): Thanks team — this thread is the source of truth for chart copy/annotations.
